name: How to Repair a Damaged Bathroom Door Frame Step by Step

step.name: Step 1: Inspect the entire opening for moisture and alignment
step.text: Check the jamb, casing, strike plate, hinges, and the subfloor right below the sill. Look closely for soft, discolored wood or active moisture from nearby showers and sinks, because enclosing damp lumber will cause rot to return quickly.

step.name: Step 2: Carefully remove the interior casing and hardware
step.text: Unscrew the door hinges to take down the door slab, then use a thin utility knife to score paint lines along the trim. Gently pry off the casing using a flat pry bar and a wood block to protect the surrounding drywall from dents.

step.name: Step 3: Cut away deteriorated jamb sections or remove the damaged frame
step.text: If the decay is limited to the bottom few inches, make a clean, horizontal oscillating saw cut above the water line. If the jamb is twisted or split across multiple hinge pockets, pull the entire jamb free from the rough opening framing.

step.name: Step 4: Treat the opening and fit moisture-resistant replacement stock
step.text: Verify that the rough wall studs are dry, sound, and clean before proceeding. Cut replacement jamb stock to exact dimensions, sealing every exposed cut edge with exterior-grade primer to block bathroom steam from wicking into the end grain.

step.name: Step 5: Set, shim, and fasten the jamb perfectly plumb
step.text: Place the new jamb in position, sliding cedar or composite shims behind hinge and strike locations until your level shows true plumb and square. Fasten through the shims into the wall framing using finish screws, checking the diagonal measurements for squareness.

step.name: Step 6: Rehang the door slab and reinstall finished trim
step.text: Mount the door slab onto the hinges and check your reveals along the top and latch sides to confirm smooth closing. Reattach the casing, set all finish nails below the surface, fill fastener holes, and apply a flexible paintable caulk along joints before final paint. If you uncover decayed framing studs or the door refuses to latch plumb, call Abraham Becerra at HH Remodeling LLC at 303-505-0866 for dependable repair support.
